q225.question: What physical conditions did the Life Carriers wait for before planting life on Urantia?
q225.answer:
The Life Carriers do not plant life arbitrarily, at any time they please. The commission of Life Carriers dispatched from Jerusem six hundred million years ago arrived on Urantia and first studied the physical conditions before initiating life [58:1.1]. They state clearly: "⟦Q 58:1.2⟧Il convient de préciser que les Porteurs de Vie ne peuvent pas instaurer la vie avant qu’une sphère ne soit mure pour l’inauguration du cycle évolutionnaire. Nous ne pouvons pas davantage provoquer un développement de la vie plus rapide que ce qui peut être supporté et assimilé par le progrès physique de la planète.⟦/Q⟧." [58:1.2] So the commission returned for a time to Jerusem, and then, five hundred and fifty million years ago, came back and planted the first life patterns in the seas [58:1.6, 58:4.2].

The conditions they waited for can be summed up under four main headings: the seas, the shorelines, the atmosphere, and the space environment.

1. Sufficiently Briny Seas

Because the Satania Life Carriers had projected a sodium chloride pattern of life, no steps could be taken until the ocean waters had become sufficiently salty. The text says: "⟦Q 58:1.3⟧Le type de protoplasme d’Urantia ne peut fonctionner que dans une solution convenablement salée.⟦/Q⟧." [58:1.3] The traces of this remain in our bodies even now: the salt solution circulating in the blood stream bathes each cell in a chemical solution essentially like the sea water that first bathed the living cells [58:1.3, 58:1.4]. Later, as the salinity of the oceans changed, living things evolved the ability to regulate the saltiness of their body fluids [58:6.5].

2. Inland Seas and Protected Bays

On a planet where life begins in the sea, the ideal conditions are provided by a large number of inland seas and a long shore line of shallow waters and sheltered bays. At that time the inland seas seldom exceeded five or six hundred feet in depth, and sunlight could penetrate to the bottom [58:1.7]. This is also why the commission waited for the continental land mass to break up further [58:1.6]. Planting life at three separate places was likewise a foresight, so that when the continents later drifted apart, each would carry life with it within its warm seas [58:4.4].

3. An Atmosphere That Protects Life

The early atmosphere was rich in carbon, ideal for plants but unable to support animal life [58:1.8]. Only toward the close of the marine-life era did the atmosphere become suited to animal respiration [59:6.10]. The atmosphere is also a shield. The ozone layer, though only about one tenth of an inch thick when reduced to the pressure at the earth's surface, screens out destructive ultraviolet rays while letting through those needed for health [58:2.2]. At night the atmosphere acts as a blanket, keeping heat from escaping too quickly [58:2.5]. The text says that there are more than forty such apparently accidental protective functions [58:2.4].

4. The Environment of Space

Space is flooded with the energy of the short space rays, an amount four hundred times greater than all other forms of radiant energy in organized space [58:3.1, 58:3.2]. These conditions of space were also related to the environment necessary for the establishment of life, and all of them had to evolve to a favorable status before the Life Carriers could actually plant life [58:3.5]. And: "⟦Q 58:3.4⟧La vie, implantée par les Porteurs de Vie, résiste entièrement à tout cet étonnant rayonnement d’énergie universelle à courte longueur d’onde.⟦/Q⟧." [58:3.4]

5. Design, Not Chance

The text says that the mechanists who regard all these conditions as accidental lack imagination. The Urantia midwayers have assembled over fifty thousand facts of physics and chemistry which they deem incompatible with the laws of accidental chance and which show the presence of intelligent purpose in the material creation [58:2.3].

Summary

The Life Carriers waited until there were sufficiently briny seas, shallow inland seas and sheltered bays, an atmosphere that protects life, and a suitably evolved space environment, and only then planted life [58:1.2, 58:1.7, 58:3.5]. Life advances only as far as the planet is prepared for it, and every one of the conditions of life that we enjoy bears the intelligent purpose of creation [58:2.3, 58:2.4].

q226.question: The Urantia Book says that new species appear "suddenly" rather than gradually. What does this mean?
q226.answer:
The Life Carriers of The Urantia Book do not regard biologic evolution as taking place only through the slow piling up of very small variations. The text says: "⟦Q 58:6.3⟧Des espèces radicalement nouvelles de vie animale surgissent d’une ère à l’autre. Ce n’est pas par suite d’une accumulation progressive de petites variations qu’elles évoluent ; elles surgissent comme ordres de vie nouveaux et parachevés, et apparaissent soudainement.⟦/Q⟧." [58:6.3] At the same time it makes plain that this is not a miracle. The sudden appearance of new species is wholly biologic and strictly natural, and there is nothing supernatural about these genetic mutations [58:6.4].

1. Gradual Change and Sudden Change Go Together

The Urantia Book does not deny gradual change. The transition from vegetable to animal life took place gradually, through many transitional stages, in the shallow seas four hundred and fifty million years ago, and all of that development was inherent in the original life patterns [58:6.1]. Living things experiment ceaselessly to adapt to an ever-changing environment [58:6.6], passing through countless gains and losses, adjustments and readjustments [58:6.8]. It is only at the moments of great leaps that a new order suddenly appears.

2. Sudden Appearances in the Geologic Record

The records of the Life Carriers give such examples again and again.
Trilobites: they appeared suddenly as the first multicellular animals, without any gradual line of ancestors [59:1.4].
Fish: when the first vertebrates, the fish, suddenly appeared from the north, the preliminary types quickly vanished [59:4.10].
Amphibians: at the height of the seas the first land animals suddenly appeared [59:5.5].
Reptiles: they appeared fully developed one hundred and forty million years ago [60:1.9].
Flowering plants and birds: the great orders of flowering plants mutated without previous gradual change [60:3.19], and the true birds also came suddenly from a reptilian group [60:3.22].
Placental mammals: they sprang directly and suddenly from a small leaping type of dinosaur [61:1.2].

3. Why There Are No "Missing Links"

From this point of view, the effort to find connecting links between the great divisions of the animal kingdom, and between the highest prehuman animals and the dawn men, will be fruitless. The text says that these so-called missing links "⟦Q 58:6.2⟧will forever remain missing, for the simple reason that they never existed⟦/Q⟧." [58:6.2] Mankind itself came from the lemur type of mammal through three successive and sudden mutations [62:0.1], and at last a mutation in the Primates stock produced two primitive human beings [61:6.2]. The six colored races also appeared by mutation within a single generation [61:7.4].

4. Trials Prepare the Next Leap

In the biologic tribulation at the end of the marine-life era, the more than one hundred thousand species dwindled to fewer than five hundred [59:6.2], but this trial left only those with survival value, to become the ancestors of the highly differentiated life of the following age [59:6.10].

5. The Body Evolves; the Mind Is Bestowed

The organs and structures of a new order of life arise in response to physical laws, but mind is not a product of physical evolution; it is a bestowal of the adjutant mind-spirits in accordance with brain capacity [58:6.7].

Summary

The word "suddenly" does not mean a miracle; it means that the potentials contained in the original life patterns are revealed all at once, through natural mutation, as full-fledged new orders [58:6.1, 58:6.3, 58:6.4]. That is why there are no connecting links between the great divisions [58:6.2], and why, upon the evolution of the body, mind is bestowed from above [58:6.7].

q227.question: Why did the dinosaurs perish, and what does it mean that "evolution will follow the growth of brains, not physical bulk"?
q227.answer:
The Urantia Book does not explain the end of the dinosaurs as a single cosmic catastrophe; it describes a process in which a type of life whose brain was far too small for its body could not find a way to survive and gradually disappeared. It sums up the lesson this way: "⟦Q 60:2.14⟧Désormais l’évolution suivra la croissance du cerveau et non la masse du corps ; le développement du cerveau caractérisera chaque époque successive de l’évolution animale et du progrès planétaire.⟦/Q⟧." [60:2.14]

1. The Appearance and Heyday of the Dinosaurs

One hundred and forty million years ago the reptiles suddenly appeared fully developed, and the dinosaurs soon became the monarchs of this age [60:1.9, 60:1.10]. The greatest event of the period beginning one hundred and twenty million years ago was the evolution and decline of the dinosaurs, which evolved in every size, from species less than two feet long to huge herbivorous dinosaurs seventy-five feet long [60:2.1]. Yet they were distinguished from all other animals in that they governed bodies weighing up to forty tons with brains weighing less than one pound [60:1.10].

2. The Cause of Their Extinction: Big Bodies, Small Brains

According to the text, these massive creatures became less active and strong as they grew larger and larger. They needed enormous amounts of food, and the land was so overrun by them that "⟦Q 60:2.3⟧they literally starved to death and became extinct—they lacked the intelligence to cope with the situation⟦/Q⟧." [60:2.3] By one hundred million years ago these all but brainless land reptiles were perishing in ever-increasing numbers [60:2.14].

3. The Dinosaurs That Went to the Water and the Air Followed the Same Path

The two species of dinosaurs that went into the water in search of food show an evolutionary retrogression [60:2.10]. These sea serpents grew to fifty feet in length, yet their brains weighed less than two ounces, and in the end they perished because they lacked the brains to protect their huge bodies [60:2.11]. The pterosaurs and flying dinosaurs, which took to the air under the fierce competition on land, likewise had too little brain for their body size and met the same fate as the dinosaurs [60:2.12, 60:3.21].

4. The Rise of Large-Brained Creatures

While the dinosaurs declined, new types appeared. Fifty-five million years ago the true birds, of the pigeon type, came suddenly from a reptilian group [60:3.22], and then in North America the placental mammals sprang suddenly from the line of a small, agile, leaping type of dinosaur [61:1.2]. The mammals had great survival advantages: they bore mature young, nurtured and protected their offspring with affection, used their superior brains for self-preservation, and employed intelligence in adapting to their environment [61:1.4-1.8]. The early mammals had large brains in proportion to their body size [61:1.10].

5. The Line That Leads to Man

This principle reaches its climax in the ancestors of mankind. The dawn mammals had large brains in proportion to their size, the mid-mammals possessed proportionately increased brain power, and then the Primates appeared [61:6.1]. Mind is not a product of physical evolution, but it is wholly dependent on the brain capacity provided by physical development [58:6.7]. The growth of brains becoming the direction of evolution was, in the end, a direction toward an ever larger vessel for receiving mind.

Summary

The dinosaurs starved to death because they lacked the intelligence to feed their enormous bodies, and their relatives that fled to the water and the air disappeared for the same reason [60:2.3, 60:2.11, 60:3.21]. After that, evolution followed brains rather than bulk, passing through birds, mammals, and Primates to man [60:2.14, 61:1.2, 61:6.1], and this was a march toward life capable of receiving higher mind [58:6.7].

q228.question: What did the ice age mean for the birth and early history of mankind?
q228.answer:
The Urantia Book portrays the ice age not as a mere climatic event but as the stage on which mankind was born and tempered. The text says, "⟦Q 61:6.1⟧Le grand évènement de cette période glaciaire fut l’apparition évolutive de l’homme primitif.⟦/Q⟧." [61:6.1] It records that the appearance of man, the emergence of the six colored races, the Lucifer rebellion, and the arrival of Adam were all interlocked with the stages of the ice age.

1. How the Ice Age Came

When the lands of northeastern North America and northern Europe were greatly elevated and ocean currents and seasonal winds shifted, snow fell almost continuously on the northern highlands, piling up to a depth of twenty thousand feet and becoming creeping ice [61:5.1, 61:5.2]. The Northern Hemisphere experienced six distinct ice invasions [61:5.4]. The first North American glacier began its southward advance two million years ago [61:5.5]. This ice age, the Pleistocene, covers a period of over two million years [61:7.17].

2. Mankind Born in a Harsh Environment

One million years ago Urantia was registered as an inhabited world, and a mutation within the Primates stock suddenly produced two primitive human beings [61:6.2]. This occurred at about the time of the beginning of the third glacial advance. So the text says, "⟦Q 61:6.3⟧thus it may be seen that your early ancestors were born and bred in a stimulating, invigorating, and difficult environment⟦/Q⟧." [61:6.3] The sole survivors of these aborigines, the Eskimos, are said even now to prefer to dwell in cold northern climes [61:6.3]. In each interglacial period man went westward around the Mediterranean and overspread Europe, and in the caves of western Europe human bones are found mingled with the remains of both tropic and arctic animals [61:6.4].

3. Milestones of Human History within the Ice Age

500,000 years ago: at the time of the fifth ice advance, the six colored races appeared by mutation within a single generation, and the Planetary Prince also arrived at this time [61:7.4].
200,000 years ago: during the advance of the last glacier, the Lucifer rebellion took place [61:7.8].
35,000 years ago: the great ice age ended except in the polar regions, approximately coinciding with the arrival of the Material Son and Daughter and the beginning of the Adamic dispensation [61:7.18].

4. A Force That Sifts and Mixes

The severe ice age exterminated many species and radically changed many others, and the migrations back and forth with the ice severely sifted the species [61:7.13]. The migrations produced an extraordinary mixture of plants and animals, and arctic species isolated on high mountains survive to this day [61:7.16]. Many of the large animals of North America became extinct at the end of the ice age [61:5.7, 61:7.15]. The first humans, Andon and Fonta, as they went northward and endured ever colder nights, discovered how to make fire with flints [63:2.5]. Mankind thus grew up in an environment that demanded adaptation.

5. Will Another Ice Age Come?

The text says that as the last glacier retreated the polar ice sheets began to form, and that as long as the polar regions are covered with ice there is little likelihood of another glacial age [61:7.11].

Summary

The ice age was the cradle in which mankind was born and raised [61:6.1, 61:6.3]. In a harsh but stimulating environment mankind appeared, and within that period came, in turn, the emergence of the colored races, the coming of the Planetary Prince, the Lucifer rebellion, and the arrival of Adam [61:7.4, 61:7.8, 61:7.18]. That an environment of trial actually tempered life is a meaningful lesson for individual life as well [61:7.13].

q229.question: In what order did the seven adjutant mind-spirits act upon evolving animals and the first human beings, and when is "human mind" said to have appeared?
q229.answer:
According to The Urantia Book, mind is not a product of physical evolution; it is a gift bestowed in turn by the seven adjutant mind-spirits as brain capacity becomes ready for it [58:6.7]. The Life Carriers testify that over the long ages of animal evolution these adjutants widened their range of action one by one, until at last "human mind" appeared when the sixth and seventh adjutants first functioned in the twins Andon and Fonta [62:6.5].

1. The Nature of the Adjutant Spirits

The seven adjutant spirits are the mind ministers to the lower intelligent existences of a local universe [65:7.1]. They are not concerned with physical evolution, which is the work of the Life Carriers, but their ministry is so perfectly integrated with the evolutionary processes of nature that people do not discern in the phenomena of mind anything other than the working of nature [65:7.2]. They do not make contact with purely mechanical responses; rather, "⟦Q 65:7.6⟧The acquisition of the potential of the ability to learn from experience marks the beginning of the functioning of the adjutant spirits⟦/Q⟧" [65:7.5, 65:7.6].

2. Five Adjutants in Animal Evolution

The observations of the Life Carriers are as follows [62:6.3].
The spirit of intuition: it first functioned in the instinctive and reflex behavior of primordial animals.
The spirit of understanding: it endowed higher types with the gift of spontaneous association of ideas.
The spirit of courage: it produced a crude form of protective self-consciousness.
The spirit of knowledge: it became evident after the appearance of the mammals.
The spirit of counsel: in the higher mammals it brought forth the herd instinct and the beginnings of primitive social development.
From the dawn mammals to the Primates the activity of these five spirits steadily increased, but the two highest adjutants had not yet functioned at all [62:6.4].

3. The Day the Spirits of Worship and Wisdom Acted

When the twins were about ten years old, the spirit of worship made its first contact with the mind of the female twin and shortly thereafter with the male. About a year later, when through meditative thought and purposeful decision they resolved to flee north, the spirit of wisdom began to function on Urantia for the first time; the text says, "⟦Q 62:6.5⟧then did the spirit of wisdom begin to function on Urantia and in these two now recognized human minds⟦/Q⟧." [62:6.5] Before this, worshipful emotions, including awe, reverence, humility, and gratitude, had suddenly appeared in the twins [62:5.4].

4. The First Decision Recognized by the Universe

On the day after the twins fled, the first test flash of the universe circuits occurred [62:7.1], and the first message from Salvington announced that the twins' decision to segregate their offspring from their inferior ancestors "⟦Q 62:7.3⟧is the first decision of mind—the human type of mind—on Urantia⟦/Q⟧" and that this decision automatically established the circuit of communication [62:7.3]. With the appearance of a will that can worship and choose to ascend, the task of the Life Carriers was finished [62:7.6].

5. Why Worship and Wisdom Come Together

Up to the sixth adjutant, the spirit of worship, the adjutants function only in the evolution of the experiencing mind, but at this level an overlapping of ministry occurs, and when the seventh adjutant, the spirit of wisdom, is active, the ministry of yet another spirit accompanies it [65:7.7]. Mind can learn by experience [65:6.8], and an organism endowed with mind can alter its very environment [65:6.9]. Just as the brain is responsive to the ministry of mind, so mind possesses a capacity for spirit receptivity [65:6.10].

Summary

The seven adjutants served animal evolution in the order of intuition, understanding, courage, knowledge, and counsel, and human mind was born when the spirits of worship and wisdom first acted in the twins [62:6.3, 62:6.5]. The marks of humanness were worshipful emotion and wise, purposeful decision, and in us too the mind opens toward spirit through worship and wise choosing [62:7.3, 65:7.7].

q230.question: Who was Onagar, the first teacher of truth, and what was the primitive religion he taught?
q230.answer:
Onagar was a great intellect and spiritual leader who arose among the retrogressing Andonites before the coming of the Planetary Prince. As the Andonites dispersed and their cultural and spiritual status slowly retrogressed for nearly ten thousand years, Onagar became the leader of the tribes, brought peace among them, and for the first time led all of them in the worship of the "⟦Q 63:6.1⟧Breath Giver to men and animals⟦/Q⟧" [63:6.1]. He was born 983,323 years before A.D. 1934 and lived to the age of sixty-nine [63:6.8].

1. The Religious Situation before Onagar

Because of the comfort that the accidentally discovered fire gave him, Andon almost came to worship fire; reason led him toward the sun, but the sun seemed too far away, and so he did not become a sun worshiper [63:6.2]. The Andonites feared natural phenomena such as thunder, lightning, rain, and ice, and hunger led them to worship the larger food animals [63:6.3]. The ceremonies that grew up around the carcass of a revered animal later developed into sacrificial rites, and the text says this was the origin of sacrifice in worship [63:6.4].

2. Onagar's Teaching: One Deity and the Great Beyond

Onagar kept his headquarters at Oban, on the northern shores of the ancient Mediterranean in the region of the present Caspian Sea, and from there he sent teachers to the remote settlements to spread "⟦Q 63:6.7⟧his new doctrines of one Deity and his concept of the hereafter, which he called the Great Beyond⟦/Q⟧" [63:6.7]. The heart of his work was turning worship away from animals and the forces of nature to the One who gives life [63:6.1].

3. Onagar's Prayer

How important food was to primitive man is shown in the prayer that he taught [63:6.5]: "⟦Q 63:6.6⟧« Ô Souffle de Vie, donne-nous aujourd’hui notre nourriture quotidienne, délivre-nous de la malédiction de la glace, sauve-nous de nos ennemis des forêts et reçois-nous avec miséricorde dans le Grand Au-delà. »⟦/Q⟧." [63:6.6] This prayer holds together daily bread, deliverance from danger, and the hope of life after death.

4. The First Missionaries and Social Organization

Onagar's emissaries were the world's first missionaries, and they were also the first human beings to cook meat and regularly to use fire in the preparation of food [63:6.7]. He organized the primitive tribes into a real society and established an efficient system of tribal government such as later generations did not attain for thousands of years. The text judges that never again until the arrival of the Planetary Prince was there so high a spiritual civilization on earth [63:6.8].

5. The Golden Age of Primitive Man and the Decline That Followed

Andon and Fonta and many of their descendants had received Thought Adjusters, but it was in the days of Onagar that the Adjusters and guardian seraphim came in great numbers to Urantia, and the text calls this "⟦Q 63:6.9⟧the golden age of primitive man⟦/Q⟧" [63:6.9]. Yet this primitive but genuine religion faded away among his retrogressing descendants [63:6.8], and by nine hundred thousand years ago the arts of Andon and Fonta and the culture of Onagar were vanishing from the face of the earth [64:2.1]. Remnants were preserved to some extent by the Foxhall peoples of England and the Badonan tribes of northwestern India [64:2.4].

Summary

Onagar was the first teacher of truth, who taught primitive men, still dwelling in fear and animal worship, about the one Deity who gives the breath of life and about the Great Beyond [63:6.1, 63:6.7]. The fact that Adjusters and seraphim came in great numbers in his time [63:6.9] shows how greatly the sincere spiritual leadership of one person can raise the spiritual receptivity of an entire age.

q231.question: What spiritual experiences did Andon and Fonta, the first parents of mankind, have, and what became of them after death?
q231.answer:
Andon and Fonta were not merely the first human beings to appear biologically; they were the first human beings to worship and to make purposeful decisions. The text calls them "⟦Q 63:1.1⟧the most remarkable pair of human beings that have ever lived on the face of the earth⟦/Q⟧" [63:1.1], and it says that the story of their evolution, struggles, death, and eternal survival is "⟦Q 63:7.4⟧the most heroic and fascinating chapter in all the history of Urantia⟦/Q⟧" [63:7.4].

1. The Meaning of Their Names

Andon is the Nebadon name which signifies "⟦Q 63:0.3⟧the first Fatherlike creature to exhibit human perfection hunger⟦/Q⟧," and Fonta signifies "⟦Q 63:0.3⟧the first Sonlike creature to exhibit human perfection hunger⟦/Q⟧" [63:0.3]. They never knew these names until their fusion with their Adjusters; on earth they called each other Sonta-an (loved by mother) and Sonta-en (loved by father), names that reflect their mutual regard and affection [63:0.3].

2. Worshipful Emotion and the First Decisions

Worshipful emotions such as awe, reverence, humility, and gratitude appeared early in the twins [62:5.4]. At about nine years of age they decided to live with and for each other, the first of a series of agreements that led to their decision to flee northward [62:5.8]. The Life Carriers could not control their minds, but within the permitted limits they guided them northward [62:5.9]. Their vague awareness of being more than mere animals came from their possession of personality and was further heightened by the indwelling of the Thought Adjusters [63:1.4].

3. Receiving the Thought Adjusters

When Andon and Fonta made the decision that made it possible for Thought Adjusters to indwell them, the twelve Melchizedek observers arrived [65:4.9]. At the time of the planet's recognition, the archangels' message closed by saying that all archangels pray that these creatures "⟦Q 63:0.2⟧may speedily be endowed with the personal indwelling of the gift of the spirit of the Universal Father⟦/Q⟧" [63:0.2]. Andon and Fonta did in fact receive Thought Adjusters, as did many of their descendants [63:6.9].

4. Life and Death on Earth

They discovered how to make fire with flints [63:2.5], had nineteen children [63:3.2], and labored unceasingly for the nurture and uplifting of their clan until, at the age of forty-two, they were killed together by falling rock during an earthquake [63:3.4]. Their descendants buried them under a heap of stones, though the concept of survival after death was then very vague [63:3.5].

5. Survival, Fusion, and Service

Andon and Fonta were recognized in the adjudication made at the arrival of the Planetary Prince, passed through the mansion world system, and became citizens of Jerusem [63:7.1]. On Jerusem they fused with their Thought Adjusters, as did several of their children, including Sontad, but most of their immediate descendants attained only spirit fusion [63:7.2]. Afterwards they were permitted to return to the first mansion world to serve in receiving the pilgrims of time [63:7.3]. They grieved over the betrayal of Caligastia and the failure of Adam, but they rejoiced greatly at the news that Michael had chosen their world as the scene of his bestowal [63:7.1].

Summary

Andon and Fonta were the parents of mankind who first showed the hunger for perfection, worshiped, made purposeful decisions, and received Thought Adjusters [63:0.3, 63:1.4, 65:4.9]. After death they survived and fused with their Adjusters, and they still welcome newly arriving mortals on the first mansion world [63:7.2, 63:7.3]. They are evidence that, even in primitive conditions, sincere longing and choice lead to eternal survival.

q232.question: How did the Foxhall peoples, the Badonites, and the Neanderthal race appear after the Andonites, and what kind of age was this?
q232.answer:
After the early culture of the Andonites declined, during the roughly five hundred thousand years until the appearance of the colored races, the earth was inhabited by the Foxhall peoples, the Badonites, and the Neanderthal race that sprang from the Badonites. The Urantia Book portrays this period as a "spiritual dark age" in which culture and religion sank to their lowest levels, yet it records that in its midst there were small lamps that kept alive the traditions of Andon and Onagar [64:2.1, 64:2.4, 64:4.12].

1. The Causes of the Decline

At first the Andonites instinctively avoided the danger of mixing with the inferior simian tribes [64:1.1], and, shunning the forests, they developed activity and invention amid cold and hunger in the open lands and higher latitudes [64:1.3]. But those who went eastward mixed freely with their inferior animal cousins, and their descendants came back and deteriorated the superior stock, while the settlements that worshiped the Breath Giver steadily dwindled [64:1.7]. By nine hundred thousand years ago the arts of Andon and Fonta and the culture of Onagar were vanishing, and culture, religion, and even flintwork reached their lowest levels [64:2.1].

2. The Foxhall Peoples: The Lamp in the West

The Foxhall peoples of England, in the farthest west, preserved comparatively much of the Andonic culture, passed on the art of flintwork to later ages, and their descendants became the ancestors of the ancient Eskimos [64:2.5]. They were the first human inhabitants of that region [64:2.6], and the more intelligent and spiritually advanced among them kept up their primitive religious practices [64:2.7].

3. The Badonites: The Lamp in the East

The Badonan tribes of the northwestern Indian highlands were the descendants of a great-great-grandson of Andon, and the text says, "⟦Q 64:3.1⟧Ces peuplades furent les seuls descendants d’Andon qui ne pratiquèrent jamais de sacrifices humains.⟦/Q⟧." [64:3.1] Having watched the Mesopotamian peninsula sink beneath the sea, they greatly feared water and chose the highlands for their home [64:3.3]. Eight hundred and fifty thousand years ago they waged a war of extermination against their inferior neighboring tribes, and their improved, mixed descendants appeared almost as a new race: these were the Neanderthal race [64:3.5].

4. The Neanderthal Race

The Neanderthalers were excellent fighters and hunters; they spread from northwestern India to France, China, and North Africa and dominated the world for almost half a million years, until the migrations of the colored races [64:4.1, 64:4.2]. Their flintwork almost reached the level of Andon's day [64:4.3], and they even caught fish through holes cut in the ice [64:4.4]. Yet for nearly two hundred and fifty thousand years there was almost no progress, and it seemed that the attempt to produce a new intelligent life had all but failed [64:4.11].

5. Religion in the Spiritual Dark Age

The Neanderthalers had no religion beyond shameful superstitions, and they greatly feared clouds and mists [64:4.12]. They were mortally afraid of darkness and began to sacrifice the finest of their men and women so that the moon would shine again [64:4.13]. This fear stands in great contrast to the faith of the days of Andon and Onagar, when men worshiped the "Breath Giver" [63:6.1].

Summary

The Foxhall peoples and the Badonites were the western and eastern centers of culture that kept alive the traditions of Andon and Onagar in an age of decline, and from the Badonites came the Neanderthal race, which dominated the world for a long time [64:2.4, 64:3.5, 64:4.1]. But this era was a spiritual dark age of fear and human sacrifice [64:4.12, 64:4.13], and the text warns that civilizations of great promise have retrogressed when superior stocks were indiscriminately mixed [64:1.8].

q233.question: What does it mean that Urantia was a "life-experiment planet," and how did it differ from ordinary worlds?
q233.answer:
Urantia was a "life-experiment world," that is, a life-modification world, on which the Life Carriers made their sixtieth attempt to modify and improve the Satania adaptation of the Nebadon life designs [65:4.1, 58:1.1]. That is why Urantia life is unique, and "⟦Q 58:4.1⟧there is no other world in all Satania, even in all Nebadon, that has a life existence just like that of Urantia⟦/Q⟧" [58:4.1]. This does not mean, however, that it was a haphazard trial. The text makes clear that the evolution of life is a progressive and variable technique, "⟦Q 65:4.2⟧but never haphazard, uncontrolled, nor wholly experimental, in the accidental sense⟦/Q⟧." [65:4.2]

1. The Results of the Experiment

On Urantia the Life Carriers achieved numerous beneficial modifications of the standard life patterns and worked out not less than twenty-eight features of life modification which will be of service to all Nebadon [65:4.1]. One example is the chemistry of wound healing and cell regeneration: the Life Carriers chose it from formulas involving more than one hundred thousand phases of chemical reaction, and they made over half a million experiments before settling on it [65:4.3, 65:4.4]. This technique was later improved when it was introduced on other worlds of Satania [65:4.6].

2. How It Differed from Ordinary Worlds

The priority of the Andonites: the Andonites appeared before the six colored races [65:4.7].
Six races from one family: the six Sangik races originated simultaneously in a single family, and Urantia is the first world in Satania where this happened [65:4.7].
An early will: ordinarily will appears only after the colored races have long existed, but Urantia is the only planet in Satania where human will appeared in a precolored race [65:4.11].
A late Planetary Prince: ordinarily the Prince arrives at about the time human will appears, but Caligastia came almost half a million years later, and in the meantime the twelve Melchizedek receivers supervised the planet [65:4.8, 65:4.9].
Life Carriers remaining: because it was a life-modification world, two senior Life Carriers and twelve assistants were permitted to remain [62:7.6].

3. Side Effects of the Experiment

The efforts to improve the patterns produced seemingly meaningless transitional forms of life [65:4.10] and numerous strange genetic by-products [65:4.12]. The adjutant mind-spirits too, being relatively isolated on a life-experiment world, met the greatest difficulty in all Nebadon in contacting the evolving organisms of Urantia [65:7.3, 65:7.4].

4. Tragedies That Disrupted the Plan

The Life Carriers regret that the betrayal of Caligastia and the default of Adam interfered with their efforts [65:5.1]. Their greatest disappointment was that some vegetable life reverted to parasitic bacteria that brought many diseases upon mankind, and the hope that an admixture of Adam's life plasm would produce immunity to them was also shattered by Adam's default [65:5.2].

5. The Attitude of the Life Carriers

Nevertheless, the Life Carriers say that the universe is not run for their convenience, and that it is fitting to co-operate patiently with the rule of wisdom and the march of progress [65:5.3]. The tribulations were followed by compensations such as Michael's bestowal, and the celestial supervisors are confident of the ultimate triumph of mankind and the vindication of the original plans [65:5.4].

Summary

Urantia was a deliberate life-modification world intended to improve the life patterns, and so it bore unique features such as an early will, six races from one family, and a late Planetary Prince [65:4.1, 65:4.7, 65:4.11]. Along with the achievements of the experiment there were confusion and tragedy, but this world in the end received Michael's bestowal, and final victory is promised [65:5.4].

q234.question: Why does the evolution of life take so long, and what lesson does it hold for our spiritual growth?
q234.answer:
The Life Carriers explain why evolution takes so long. They cannot time the life processes to unfold any faster than the physical metamorphoses of the planet will permit, and they have absolutely no control over geologic evolution. They even say, "⟦Q 65:8.2⟧Si les conditions physiques le permettaient, nous pourrions prendre nos dispositions pour parachever l’évolution complète de la vie en beaucoup moins d’un million d’années.⟦/Q⟧." [65:8.2] The length of time comes not from any incapacity of the Life Carriers but from a universe order in which matter, mind, and spirit each await their own readiness [65:8.1, 65:8.5].

1. The Physical Conditions Must Be Ready First

From the beginning the Life Carriers said that they cannot initiate life until a sphere is ripe, nor develop life faster than the planet can support [58:1.2]. Even after implanting life, they waited until the continents broke up and the seas became suitable [58:1.6]. "⟦Q 65:8.1⟧Temps et espace sont indissolublement liés ; c’est une association innée. Les délais du temps sont inévitables en présence de certaines conditions de l’espace.⟦/Q⟧." [65:8.1]

2. Time Seems Long According to the Life Span of the Observer

Since a creature's standard of time is the length of its own life, every creature regards evolution as a long and delayed process. But to beings whose life span is not limited by temporal existence, evolution does not seem so long, and on Paradise time does not exist; everything is present [65:8.3]. The Life Carriers themselves are under the jurisdiction of the Supreme Rulers of Paradise, where time is nonexistent [65:8.2].

3. Mind Waits on Matter, Spirit Waits on Mind

The text says that the same principle applies to spiritual growth. As mind evolution depends on the slow development of physical conditions, so spiritual progress depends on mental expansion and is delayed by intellectual retardation [65:8.4]. This does not mean that the evolution of the soul depends on education or culture. The soul may evolve regardless of mental culture, but not without the choice of survival and the decision to do the will of the Father in heaven. The text concludes: "⟦Q 65:8.4⟧Bien que la survie puisse ne pas dépendre de la possession de la connaissance et de la sagesse, la progression en dépend très certainement.⟦/Q⟧." [65:8.4]

4. No Obstacle Can Defeat a Sincere Choice

Mind is always dominant over matter and spirit is ever correlated with mind, and when these endowments fail to co-ordinate, time delays may result. But if anyone sincerely desires to know God, to find him, and to become like him, survival is assured regardless of the handicaps of time. Physical status and mental perversity may delay spiritual attainment, "⟦Q 65:8.5⟧but none of these obstacles can defeat the whole-souled choice of will⟦/Q⟧." [65:8.5]

5. When the Time Is Ripe, Change Comes Quickly

When physical conditions are ripe, sudden mind evolution may take place, and when mind is ready, spiritual transformation may also occur rapidly [65:8.6]. Just as new species appear suddenly in the geologic record [58:6.3], so in spiritual life too there are leaps after long preparation. Moreover, all life is pervaded by an unsatisfied longing for perfection and an innate seeking instinct [65:6.2].

Summary

Evolution takes so long because life must wait for the physical preparation of the planet, and because time and space are inherently linked [65:8.1, 65:8.2]. By the same principle, spiritual growth may also be slow as it waits for the readiness of mind, but the sincere choice of will to seek God is defeated by no delay, and when the readiness comes, change comes quickly [65:8.4-8.6]. The lesson of this teaching, then, is not to be impatient but to grow with patience [65:5.3].

q235.question: Are we still spiritually harmed today because of Caligastia's rebellion and Adam's default? Please explain the "far-flung repercussions of sin."
q235.answer:
The answer of The Urantia Book is clear. The rebellion and the default greatly delayed the material, social, and intellectual progress of this planet, but no mortal born afterward has ever suffered loss in his personal spiritual experience because of them. The text says, "⟦Q 67:7.7⟧Nul ne subit jamais une privation spirituelle essentielle à cause du péché d’autrui.⟦/Q⟧." [67:7.7] The key to this distinction lies in separating the personal and the impersonal consequences of sin.

1. The Two Kinds of Consequences of Sin

The personal (centripetal) consequences that follow the deliberate and persistent rejection of light are inevitable and wholly individual; they concern only God and his creature. The soul-destroying harvest of iniquity is reaped within the iniquitous creature himself [67:7.1]. On the other hand, the outward repercussions of sin, its impersonal (centrifugal) consequences, are inevitable and collective, reaching every being within the range of influence of the event [67:7.2].

2. The Collective Damage Urantia Suffered

After the rebellion Caligastia tried to reconstruct society at once by a premature application of his doctrines of liberty, but this quickly failed, and society retrogressed to its old biologic level [67:5.3]. Dalamatia eventually sank beneath the sea [67:5.4]. Even fifty thousand years after the collapse of the administration, mankind had made little progress compared with the time of Caligastia's arrival [67:7.3]. Sin hardly delayed biologic evolution, but it robbed mankind of the full benefit of the Adamic inheritance and enormously retarded intellectual development, moral growth, social progress, and mass spiritual attainment [67:7.6]. The Life Carriers also say that the hope that Adam's life plasm would provide immunity to disease was shattered by Adam's default [65:5.2].

3. Why Sin Is Never Purely Local

The text explains that the administrative sectors of the universe are organismal, so that "⟦Q 67:7.4⟧the plight of one personality must to a certain extent be shared by all⟦/Q⟧." [67:7.4] But the full consequences of erroneous thinking or planning are experienced only on the level of actual performance, and sin becomes fatal to personality survival only when it is the attitude of the whole being, the choosing of the mind and the willing of the soul [67:7.4].

4. No One's Sin Can Prevent My Survival

Evil and sin bring their consequences in material and social realms and may even retard spiritual progress on certain levels, "⟦Q 67:7.5⟧but never does the sin of any being rob another of the realization of the divine right of personality survival⟦/Q⟧." [67:7.5] Eternal survival can be jeopardized only by the decisions of one's own mind and the choice of one's own soul [67:7.5]. Every mortal born since the rebellion has been time-penalized, but the future welfare of those souls has never been in the least eternity-jeopardized [67:7.7]. Sin is wholly personal as to moral guilt and spiritual consequences; only its administrative, intellectual, and social repercussions are far-flung [67:7.7].

5. Individuals Who Shone Even in the Age of Rebellion

As if to prove this principle, even in the time of the rebellion human heroes such as Amadon remained loyal [67:8.1], and sin could not prevent the supreme spiritual attainment of individuals who sought to know God and do his will [67:7.6]. The text adds that, although we cannot fully understand the wisdom that permits such catastrophes, we can discern the ultimate good that local confusion brings to the universe as a whole [67:7.8].

Summary

The impersonal repercussions of sin are collective, and they long held back the civilization and the spiritual atmosphere of Urantia [67:7.2, 67:7.6]. But the personal consequences of sin and eternal survival depend wholly on individual choice, so the errors of Caligastia and Adam cannot block the way by which each of us today seeks God and survives [67:7.5, 67:7.7]. This is a teaching not of the burden of "original sin" but of personal responsibility and hope.

q236.question: What led primitive man to form society, and what role did "ghost fear" play in civilization?
q236.answer:
The Urantia Book says that human beings did not form society because they naturally loved to gather in friendship. Primitive man was not naturally overflowing with the spirit of brotherly feeling, and the early races learned by sad experience that "⟦Q 68:1.1⟧in union there is strength⟦/Q⟧" [68:1.1]. The text sums up the forces that built society in four: "⟦Q 68:3.4⟧Hunger and love drove men together; vanity and ghost fear held them together⟦/Q⟧." [68:3.4]

1. Fear of Isolation and Survival

Solidarity was early the price of survival. A lone man without a tribal mark was helpless, and civilization became man's insurance against violent death [68:1.2]. Primitive society was built on mutual need and the security that association gave [68:1.3], and men first learned to co-operate out of fear and later co-operate because they discover it to be most beneficial [68:1.4]. Civilization is a racial acquirement that is not biologically inherited, so each generation must be newly educated [68:0.2].

2. Hunger and Sex Love

The two great forces that first brought human beings together were food hunger and sex love [68:2.4]. The text says, "⟦Q 68:2.5⟧L’histoire n’est que le compte rendu de la lutte millénaire des hommes pour leur nourriture.⟦/Q⟧," and that food saving was primitive man's first self-denial [68:2.5]. The sex urge alone could not hold the home together; the early home was built on woman's devoted mother love and on the need for food [68:2.6, 68:2.7]. The family was the first successful peace group [68:2.8].

3. Vanity

Vanity, including pride, ambition, and honor, held people together because it needs an audience before which to display itself, and it became the early origin of all the arts, ceremonies, and games [68:2.10]. But the text warns that pleasure-want has superseded hunger-want, and "⟦Q 68:2.11⟧La préservation du moi édifie la société ; le déchainement des satisfactions égoïstes détruit infailliblement la civilisation.⟦/Q⟧." [68:2.11]

4. Ghost Fear

Common fear was physiological, such as fear of pain or hunger, "⟦Q 68:3.1⟧but ghost fear was a new and sublime sort of terror⟦/Q⟧" [68:3.1]. The text counts the ghost dream as probably the greatest single factor in the social evolution of mankind. Ghost dreams bound people together for mutual protection against unseen dangers, and they marked one of the earliest differences between the animal and the human mind, since animals do not imagine survival after death [68:3.2]. This fear whipped the loose social orders into more thoroughly disciplined and better controlled groups [68:3.3].

5. From Fear to Awe

This senseless superstition prepared the minds of men for the later discovery of "⟦Q 68:3.3⟧the fear of the Lord which is the beginning of wisdom⟦/Q⟧," and the text says: "⟦Q 68:3.3⟧Les peurs sans fondement dues à l’évolution sont destinées à être supplantées par le respect craintif de la Déité inspiré par la révélation.⟦/Q⟧." [68:3.3] Yet these four emotions alone cannot endure the strain of society, and without help from superhuman sources they actually plunge mankind into war [68:3.4]. Mankind's peaceful tendencies are not innate; they come from revealed religion and accumulated experience, especially from the teachings of Jesus, the Prince of Peace [68:3.5].

Summary

Primitive society was gathered by hunger and sex love and held together by vanity and ghost fear [68:2.4, 68:3.4]. Ghost fear in particular bound society firmly together and prepared the human mind to be led toward awe for Deity [68:3.2, 68:3.3], but true peace and brotherhood come not from the emotions of evolution but from revelation and the teachings of Jesus [68:3.5].

q237.question: How does The Urantia Book evaluate primitive institutions such as slavery, capital, and private property?
q237.answer:
The Urantia Book neither simply praises nor simply condemns human institutions on moral grounds; it looks both at what social need each one met at its stage of evolution and at what it must now give way to. The starting point is this principle: every human institution ministers to some social need, but its overdevelopment detracts from the worth of the individual, and so "⟦Q 69:1.1⟧L’homme devrait contrôler ses institutions et non se laisser dominer par ces créations d’une civilisation qui progresse.⟦/Q⟧." [69:1.1]

1. The Three Classes of Institutions

Human institutions fall into institutions of self-maintenance (industry, property, and the regulative agencies of society), institutions of self-perpetuation (marriage and the home, schools, education, ethics, and religion), and institutions of self-gratification (adornment, amusement, and games) [69:1.3-1.5]. Fear, ignorance, and superstition played a prominent part in the early origin of all institutions [69:1.3], and the three classes are interdependent, functioning as one social mechanism [69:1.6].

2. Slavery: A Necessary but Most Harmful Link

In primitive times captives were eaten, killed, or sacrificed, so slavery was in fact "⟦Q 69:8.2⟧a great advancement over massacre and cannibalism⟦/Q⟧." [69:8.2] The text calls slavery "⟦Q 69:8.6⟧an indispensable link in the chain of human civilization⟦/Q⟧" and the bridge over which society passed from chaos to order [69:8.6], and it says that slavery became the beginning of government [69:8.7]. Man learned industry in the schools of oppression, but slavery "⟦Q 69:8.8⟧soon insidiously attacks society internally as the gravest of all destructive social maladies⟦/Q⟧." [69:8.8] The invention of machinery made the slave obsolete [69:8.9], yet even today many people become slaves of debt through ambition [69:8.10].

3. Capital: Renouncing the Present for the Future

"⟦Q 69:5.1⟧Le capital est un travail comportant renonciation au présent en faveur de l’avenir.⟦/Q⟧," and food hoarding developed self-control [69:5.1]. The motives for accumulating capital included foresight, love of family, vanity, social position, power, and ghost fear [69:5.4-5.9]. Capital has been abused, but it is the foundation of modern industrial society, and thanks to capital and invention the present generation enjoys more liberty than any before it [69:5.15].

4. Primitive Communism and Private Property

Primitive communism prevented extreme poverty, but it fostered idleness and stifled industry and ambition, and because it ran counter to four tendencies, the family, religious leanings, the desire for liberty and leisure, and the urge for security and power, it gave way to a higher order [69:9.1, 69:9.2]. Private property was at first respected because of the superstition that something of the owner's personality resided in it [69:9.9], and it brought increased liberty and enhanced stability [69:9.16]. But "⟦Q 69:9.17⟧Le droit de propriété n’est pas absolu ; il est purement social.⟦/Q⟧." [69:9.17]

5. Wisdom about Change

The Melchizedek says that the present social order is not sacred, but that mankind would do well to make changes slowly, to make sure when it changes that it is changing for the better, and not to experiment again with formulas that its forebears discarded [69:9.18]. The social ideal is universal freedom, but idleness should never be tolerated [69:8.11].

Summary

Slavery, capital, and private property all played a necessary role at a certain stage of civilization, but none of them is absolute or sacred [69:8.6, 69:9.17]. Slavery is the most harmful institution and must disappear; capital and property have widened liberty, but their abuse must be guarded against [69:8.8, 69:5.15]. Man must control his institutions, and change should move forward, but carefully [69:1.1, 69:9.18].

q238.question: How did war begin, what social value did it have in the past, and why must it now disappear?
q238.answer:
The Urantia Book regards war neither as the inescapable fate of human nature nor as nothing but pure evil. The text says, "⟦Q 70:1.1⟧La guerre est l’état naturel et l’héritage de l’homme en évolution ; la paix est l’étalon social mesurant le développement de la civilisation.⟦/Q⟧." [70:1.1] Because war is the heritage of man evolved from the animal, it has persisted long, but it is an outworn method that must be replaced by better substitutes as civilization advances [70:1.7, 70:2.9].

1. The Origin of War

War is an animal reaction to misunderstandings and irritations, while peace comes from solving such problems in a civilized way [70:1.2]. The Andonites learned the golden rule early, and Andon taught his children to settle their disputes by striking trees with sticks [70:1.2, 70:1.3]. When social groups arose, peace was enjoyed only within the in-group, and outsiders were hated [70:1.5].

2. The Seven Causes of Early War

The text lists the causes as follows [70:1.8-1.14].
Hunger: food raids and the shortage of land.
Woman scarcity: the stealing of women always caused war.
Vanity: the desire to display tribal prowess.
Slaves: the recruiting of the labor class.
Revenge: retaliation for the death of a fellow tribesman.
Recreation: to young men, war was a sport.
Religion: all primitive religions sanctioned war, and the effort to separate church and state was one of the great peace movements.
The text makes clear that such atrocities were not instigated by the Gods [70:1.16].

3. The Gradual Refinement of War

The first refinement of war was the taking of prisoners, and then women and noncombatants were exempted [70:1.20]. The declaration of war, truces near shrines or on holy days, and the recognition of the right of asylum show the growth of a sense of fairness [70:1.21].

4. The Social Value of War in the Past

War enforced discipline and co-operation, put a premium on courage, solidified nationalism, eliminated weak peoples, and dissolved the illusion of primitive equality [70:2.3-2.8]. The needs of national defense gave rise to many social innovations [70:2.2]. But the text says, "⟦Q 70:2.1⟧War is strong medicine, very costly and most dangerous⟦/Q⟧" [70:2.1]. War should also be respected as the school of experience that taught arrogant individualists to submit to authority [70:2.21].

5. Why It Must Now Disappear

Ancient wars reduced inferior peoples, but modern conflict selectively destroys the finest stocks and destroys culture [70:2.9]. Just as physicians found better remedies than bloodletting, so international bloodletting must give way to better methods [70:2.10]. The text says not to glorify war but to discern what war has done and to provide substitutes for it, warning that without adequate substitutes war will long continue [70:2.19, 70:2.20]. Even the search for leaders must now turn to the conquests of peace, such as industrial, scientific, and social achievement [70:2.21].

Summary

War began from animal and primitive impulses such as hunger, vanity, revenge, and religion, and in the past it was a bitter medicine that gave discipline and cohesion [70:1.7, 70:2.3]. But today war destroys civilization and the best of mankind, and so it is an institution to be abolished by wisely providing peaceful substitutes [70:2.9, 70:2.19]. Peace is not innate; it is a fruit of civilization nurtured by revelation and the teachings of Jesus [68:3.5].

q239.question: The Urantia Book says that human rights and justice are not "natural." Then how did rights and law come into being?
q239.answer:
The Urantia Book explains human rights and justice not as something nature gave from the beginning but as social achievements built up by mankind through long experience. The text says, "⟦Q 70:9.1⟧La nature ne confère aucun droit à l’homme, elle ne lui donne que la vie et un monde où la vivre.⟦/Q⟧," and that "⟦Q 70:9.1⟧Le don primordial que la société fait aux hommes est la sécurité.⟦/Q⟧." [70:9.1] This is not meant to make light of rights; it is a reminder of how dearly they have been won, and that they must be continually guarded and refined.

1. The Rights Society Guarantees

The text lists ten rights that society has gradually asserted: the provision of food, military defense, internal peace, marriage and the family, property, the fostering of competition, the education of youth, trade and industry, the improvement of labor conditions, and the freedom of religious practices. The last is meant to exalt all the other social activities by spiritual motivation [70:9.3-9.12].

2. Rights Are "⟦Q 70:9.13⟧the Rules of the Game⟦/Q⟧"

When rights are so old that their origin is unknown, they are called natural rights, "⟦Q 70:9.13⟧Cependant, les droits humains ne sont pas réellement naturels ; ils sont entièrement sociaux.⟦/Q⟧." [70:9.13] Rights are relative and ever changing, the recognized adjustments of relations governing human competition, that is, the rules of the game [70:9.13]. In medieval Europe there were scarcely any recognized human rights, and in reaction to this arose the belief that all men are born equal, which the text also regards as an error [70:9.15]. The ideal of equality is the child of civilization; it is not found in nature [70:9.17].

3. The Evolution of Justice

Nature provides but one kind of justice, the inevitable conformity of results to causes [70:10.1]. Justice, as man conceives it, means getting one's rights; the concept may be constitutive in the spirit-endowed mind, but it does not spring full-fledged into existence [70:10.2]. In case of death primitive man asked, "⟦Q 70:10.3⟧not what killed him, but who?⟦/Q⟧" and motive was disregarded [70:10.3]. There were trials by poison and by fire [70:10.5], and the blood feud of an eye for an eye long persisted, but revealed religion taught that vengeance belongs to the Lord [70:10.9]. The text says, "⟦Q 70:10.13⟧L’administration de la véritable justice date du moment où la revanche fut enlevée aux groupes privés et apparentés pour être confiée aux soins du groupe social, l’État.⟦/Q⟧." [70:10.13] Men also learned that the certainty and swiftness of punishment are a better deterrent than its severity [70:10.15].

4. From Mores to Law

Mores are "⟦Q 70:11.1⟧laws and police regulations in the making⟦/Q⟧" [70:11.1]. Law is at first prohibitive and becomes increasingly positive in advanced civilizations [70:11.2]. Self-interest established the taboo against killing, society made it into mores, and religion sanctified it as moral law, making human life more secure [70:11.5]. Law is the codified record of long human experience [70:11.6]. The text says that the status of a civilization is very accurately shown by the fairness of its courts and the integrity of its judges [70:11.14].

5. Government That Guards Liberty

Evolutionary peoples are best governed by representative government in which the powers of the executive, legislative, and judicial branches are balanced [70:12.1]. The mortals of Urantia are entitled to liberty [70:12.5], and the charter of liberty must be wisely interpreted to guard against usurpation of power, demagogues, dictators, the union of church and state, the loss of personal liberty, and the like [70:12.6-12.18].

Summary

Rights and justice were not given by nature; they are rules that society has established through long trial and error [70:9.13, 70:10.2]. This evolution, from revenge to the justice of the state, from taboos and mores to written law, and from dictatorship to balanced representative government, must continue [70:10.13, 70:11.6, 70:12.1], and above it religious freedom exalts all activities spiritually [70:9.12].

q240.question: What does The Urantia Book say are the ideal state and the conditions of an advancing civilization?
q240.answer:
The Melchizedek of The Urantia Book does not regard the state as an institution of divine origin. The text says, "⟦Q 71:0.1⟧L’ÉTAT marque une évolution utile de la civilisation ; il représente le gain net que la société a retiré des ravages et des souffrances de la guerre.⟦/Q⟧." [71:0.1] The state did not come from a divine origin, nor was it designed by volition; it is a purely evolutionary institution [71:0.2]. Therefore the worth of a state depends less on its form than on what it does for its citizens.

1. Function over Form

The form of government is of little consequence provided it affords the liberty, security, education, and social co-ordination necessary for the progress of its citizens, and the text says, "⟦Q 71:3.1⟧Le cours de l’évolution sociale est déterminé par ce que l’État fait, et non par ce qu’il est.⟦/Q⟧." [71:3.1] Moreover, no state can transcend the moral values of its citizenry as shown in their leaders [71:3.1]. National selfishness and the doctrine of a chosen people were used in nation building, but no state can attain ideal levels until every form of intolerance has been overcome [71:3.2].

2. Three Impulses That Move the Ideal State

The ideal state is moved by three co-ordinated impulses [71:3.3-3.6].
Love loyalty: derived from the realization of human brotherhood.
Intelligent patriotism: based on wise ideals.
Cosmic insight: insight interpreted in terms of planetary facts, needs, and goals.
The laws of the ideal state are few in number, and it passes out of the age of taboos into an age of positive liberty founded on self-control [71:3.7]. The text says, "⟦Q 71:3.9⟧Le meilleur État est celui qui coordonne le plus en gouvernant le moins.⟦/Q⟧." [71:3.9]

3. The Service and Self-Respect of Citizens

A moral society should preserve the self-respect of its citizens and give every normal individual the opportunity for self-realization [71:3.9]. Public service is at first undertaken as a duty, but later it is sought as the greatest honor [71:3.10]. In advanced states political service is esteemed as the highest devotion of citizens [71:3.12]. On the other hand, no society that has permitted idleness or tolerated poverty has made much progress [71:3.8].

4. The Twelve Programs of an Advancing Civilization

The text lists the preservation of individual liberty, the protection of the home, economic security, the prevention of disease, compulsory education, compulsory employment, the profitable utilization of leisure, the care of the unfortunate, race improvement, the promotion of science and art, philosophy and wisdom, and the augmentation of cosmic insight, that is, spirituality [71:4.2-4.14]. These lead directly to the social achievement of the brotherhood of man and the personal status of God-consciousness [71:4.15]. True brotherhood means a social order in which all are glad to bear one another's burdens and practice the golden rule [71:4.16].

5. The Stages of Evolution of the State and Its Divine Principle

The only divine feature of human government is its division into the three domains of executive, legislative, and judicial functions, and the universe too is administered in accordance with this plan of separation [71:8.1]. The state system advances through threefold government, freedom of activity, the abolition of slavery, universal education, the conquest of disease by science, the due equality of the sexes, a universal language, the end of war and international adjudication, a worldwide vogue for the pursuit of wisdom, and the evolution of a world religion [71:8.3-8.14]. The last stage heralds the entrance of the planet into light and life [71:8.14]. The text says that Urantia is far from this ideal, but that mankind is marching toward a higher destiny [71:8.15].

Summary

The ideal state is judged not by divine authority but by what it does for its citizens; it is moved by love loyalty, intelligent patriotism, and cosmic insight, and it governs least while co-ordinating most [71:3.1, 71:3.3, 71:3.9]. At its end lie the brotherhood of man, God-consciousness, and the age of light and life [71:4.15, 71:8.14].

q241.question: What kind of society is the "government on a neighboring planet" described in Paper 72 of The Urantia Book, and what lessons does it hold for us?
q241.answer:
Paper 72 is the account in which a Melchizedek, by special permission, describes the social and political life of the most advanced race on a neighboring planet of Satania [72:0.1]. On this planet the Planetary Prince was disloyal at the time of the Lucifer rebellion, the Material Son also defaulted, and no magisterial Son has ever been bestowed, so it remained isolated; it is the world whose history is most like that of Urantia [72:0.2, 72:0.3]. Even under these unfavorable conditions, a very superior civilization is evolving on one continent about the size of Australia [72:1.1]. The account was given with the purpose of promoting the progress of civilization and the evolution of government on Urantia [72:12.3].

1. Political Organization

The central government is a federation of one hundred comparatively free states [72:2.1], and the federal government consists of three equal branches: executive, legislative, and judicial [72:2.3]. The legislature is made up of an upper house elected according to economic function, a lower house elected by social and philosophic groups, and a third house of elder statesmen of civic service [72:2.4-2.7]. Besides the courts of law there are separate socioeconomic courts: the parental courts, the educational courts, and the industrial courts [72:2.13-2.16]. Candidates for public office are limited to graduates of the state training schools [72:9.1].

2. Home and Education

These people regard the home as the basic institution of their civilization, and they look to the home for the most valuable part of a child's education and character training [72:3.4]. Attendance at the parental schools is compulsory for both parents [72:3.2], and religious training is the privilege of parents as a part of home life [72:3.5]. The chief purpose of education is to make every pupil a self-supporting citizen [72:4.5], and every student graduating at eighteen is a skilled artisan [72:4.6].

3. Industry and Social Security

Slavery was abolished without economic upheaval by a gradual emancipation of two per cent each year [72:5.2]. Violence has been outlawed as a means of settling disputes [72:5.3], and the industrial courts fix the compensation for capital, management, and labor and then divide the excess earnings proportionately among the three [72:5.4-5.8]. The profit motive is being replaced by higher motives [72:5.10], and the people have begun to despise idleness and unearned income [72:5.12]. Instead of charity that wounds self-respect, they provide dignified old-age insurance [72:6.1], and betrayal of a public trust is punished more severely than any crime except treason and murder [72:6.9].

4. Defense and Peace

This nation maintains a powerful defense, but it has not waged an offensive war in over one hundred years, and the text credits them: "⟦Q 72:11.4⟧Ces gens se sont civilisés au point où ils peuvent vigoureusement défendre la civilisation sans céder à la tentation d’employer leur potentiel de guerre à des agressions.⟦/Q⟧." [72:11.4] At the same time they pay far more attention to the training of statesmen, scientists, and philosophers [72:11.4].

5. Its Limits and the Lessons for Urantia

This society is not perfect either. The other ten continents beyond this one are inferior to the advanced nations of Urantia [72:12.1], and the Melchizedek fears that they may make the mistake of forcing their superior culture and religion on other peoples [72:12.2]. And he stresses that Urantia has a great advantage they lack. That sister sphere has not had the benefit of the bestowals of the Paradise Sons [72:12.4], but "⟦Q 72:12.5⟧The pouring out of the Spirit of Truth provides the spiritual foundation for the realization of great achievements in the interests of the human race of the bestowal world⟦/Q⟧." [72:12.5] Urantia is therefore far better prepared to realize world peace under law and a planetary government [72:12.5].

Summary

The continental nation of the neighboring planet, under the same handicaps of rebellion and default, has achieved a high civilization through home-centered education, balanced representative government, a fair industrial order, and a defensive military power [72:2.3, 72:3.4, 72:5.8, 72:11.4]. Urantia, having received Michael's bestowal and the Spirit of Truth, has a greater spiritual foundation, and so, taking this example as a mirror, it can move toward peace under law and the age of light and life [72:12.4, 72:12.5].

q242.question: Did the "tree of life" in the Garden of Eden really exist? Please explain its origin, its role, and its end.
q242.answer:
The Urantia Book distinguishes the two trees of Genesis. The text says, "⟦Q 73:6.3⟧The 'tree of the knowledge of good and evil' may be a figure of speech, a symbolic designation covering a multitude of human experiences⟦/Q⟧," but the tree of life "⟦Q 73:6.3⟧was not a myth; it was real and for a long time was present on Urantia⟦/Q⟧." [73:6.3] This tree was a special plant that, from the time of Caligastia until the fall of the Garden of Eden, enabled superhuman beings in material bodies to live long on earth.

1. Origin: A Shrub from Edentia

When the Most Highs of Edentia approved the commission of Caligastia as Planetary Prince and of the one hundred Jerusem citizens as his staff, "⟦Q 73:6.3⟧they sent to the planet, by the Melchizedeks, a shrub of Edentia, and this plant grew to be the tree of life on Urantia⟦/Q⟧." [73:6.3] This form of nonintelligent life is native to the constellation headquarters spheres; it is also found on the headquarters worlds of the local and superuniverses and on the Havona spheres, but not on the system capitals [73:6.3]. In the days of Dalamatia this tree grew in the center of the central court of the Father's temple [66:4.13].

2. The Working of the Tree: A Superchemical Storage Battery

This superplant stored up space-energies that were antidotal to the age-producing elements of animal existence, and "⟦Q 73:6.4⟧Le fruit de l’arbre de vie agissait comme une batterie d’accumulateurs superchimiques, libérant mystérieusement, lorsqu’on le mangeait, la force prolongatrice de vie de l’univers.⟦/Q⟧." [73:6.4] But this sustenance was wholly useless to ordinary evolutionary beings; it was specifically serviceable only to the one hundred materialized members of the staff and to the one hundred modified Andonites who had contributed their life plasm to them [73:6.4]. The Material Sons on the system capital have no need of this tree; they depend on this aid to physical immortality only when repersonalized on a planet [73:6.2].

3. The Tree Guarded in the Age of Rebellion

When the rebellion broke out, loyal cherubim and seraphim, with the help of three midwayers, guarded the tree of life, and only the loyal staff and their modified mortal associates were allowed to partake of its fruit and leaves [67:3.5]. Van and his associates nurtured the tree to grow again, and this shrub was taken to their highland retreat, where for more than one hundred and fifty thousand years it sustained the lives of Van and Amadon [73:6.5, 67:6.4].

4. The Tree of Life in the Garden of Eden

Van planted the tree of life in the center of the Garden temple, "⟦Q 73:6.1⟧whose leaves were for the 'healing of the nations,'⟦/Q⟧" and Adam and Eve too had to depend on this gift once they appeared in material form [73:6.1]. Adam and Eve periodically partook of its fruit in order to maintain their dual physical life form [73:6.6]. Each time they tasted the fruit, the archangel custodian warned them not to combine good and evil as Caligastia suggested: "⟦Q 75:4.4⟧In the day that you commingle good and evil, you shall surely become as the mortals of the realm; you shall surely die⟦/Q⟧." [75:4.4] After the default, access to this source of energy was denied them [75:7.6].

5. The End of the Tree

When Adam's family left the Garden, they were not permitted to take the core of the tree with them [73:6.7]. The Nodites who invaded Eden were told that by eating its fruit they would become as gods, and they ate it for many years, but because they lacked the complementary endowment it had no effect on them. In their enraged civil strife both the temple and the tree were destroyed by fire [73:6.7]. From that time on, all flesh on Urantia has gone the natural way of death and has belonged to the ascension plan that continues in the resurrection on the mansion worlds [73:6.8].

Summary

The tree of life was a real shrub sent from Edentia; it stored space-energies that counteracted aging and prolonged the lives of beings who possessed a special complement of life, such as the Prince's staff, Van and Amadon, and Adam and Eve [73:6.3, 73:6.4, 73:6.5]. It had no effect on ordinary human beings, and after the default it was burned by the Nodites [73:6.7]. The path of us mortals is not physical immortality by means of a tree but resurrection and ascension after death [73:6.8].

q243.question: How did the default of Adam and Eve come about, and what was the essence of their mistake?
q243.answer:
The default of Adam and Eve was not open rebellion or a sin of pleasure; it was a mistake of "impatience," an attempt, out of the good motive of wanting to help the world quickly, to hasten the divine plan by a short cut. The text says, "⟦Q 75:1.6⟧But they would have sometime met with success had they been more farseeing and patient. Both of them, especially Eve, were altogether too impatient⟦/Q⟧" [75:1.6].

1. A Task That Seemed Almost Hopeless

On Urantia, wounded and isolated by the rebellion, Adam's mission was a tremendous task [75:1.1]. The defective stocks had never been purged [75:1.2], religious belief and language all had to be begun anew, and the text says that no Adam was ever placed on a more difficult world [75:1.3]. After the Melchizedeks departed, they were weighed down by loneliness, and at times their courage weakened and their faith wavered [75:1.4].

2. Caligastia's Flank Attack

Caligastia visited the Garden often, but Adam and Eve were firm against every proposal of compromise, and he had no power to influence individuals against their will [75:2.1]. So he turned to Eve instead of Adam and decided to make use of the upper classes of the Nodites, the descendants of his former staff [75:2.3]. The Melchizedeks had warned Eve never to leave the side of her mate and never to attempt any private or secret methods, and she kept this for more than a hundred years, but she did not realize the danger as her visits with the Nodite leader Serapatatia became increasingly private [75:2.4].

3. Serapatatia's Plan and Eve's Consent

Serapatatia was an honest and sincere collaborator, and he never knew that he was being used as a tool of Caligastia [75:3.3, 75:3.6]. While they waited for the violet race to increase, he suggested to Eve that if the Nodites could have a leader partly of the violet stock, the peoples could be bound more firmly to the Garden [75:3.5]. After a plan that ripened in secret for more than five years, Eve met the Nodite leader Cano, and, influenced by flattery, enthusiasm, and persuasion, she consented to add her own small plan to the greater divine plan [75:3.7, 75:3.9].

4. The Essence of the Mistake: A Good Motive, a Wrong Method

The text defines good, sin, and evil this way: good is the carrying out of the divine plans; sin is a deliberate transgression of the divine will; evil is the misadaptation of plans and the maladjustment of techniques [75:4.3]. This plan was carried out in all sincerity and from the highest motives, but it was a wrong method of attaining a righteous goal, and because it departed from the divine plan, it constituted evil [75:4.6]. Gabriel judged them guilty of default, of violating the covenant of their trust, but the judges of Salvington absolved them of the charges of contempt of the universe government and of rebellion [75:7.1, 75:7.2]. They did evil, but they did not commit contempt of truth or knowingly join in rebellion [75:7.7].

5. Adam's Choice and the Tragic Consequences

To share Eve's fate, Adam deliberately chose the same error, without having been deceived [75:5.2]. The enraged Garden people annihilated the Nodite settlement, Serapatatia took his own life [75:5.3, 75:5.4], and a long war between the Adamites and the Nodites began [75:5.9]. Adam gave up the Garden without resistance and departed [75:6.2], and more than two thirds of his children went to Edentia [75:6.3]. The two of them were degraded to the status of mortals [75:7.3].

Summary

The default of Adam and Eve came about when, worn out by loneliness and impatience on an extremely difficult world, they accepted Caligastia's suggestion, which came in through a sincere collaborator, and tried to hasten the divine plan by a short cut [75:1.6, 75:2.3, 75:3.9]. The text leaves this lesson: on the way to perfection, "⟦Q 75:8.5⟧Never, in all your ascent to Paradise, will you gain anything by impatiently attempting to circumvent the established and divine plan by short cuts, personal inventions, or other devices⟦/Q⟧" [75:8.5].

q244.question: The Urantia Book says there was no "fall of man." Then what did the default of Adam and Eve leave to mankind, and what became of them?
q244.answer:
The Urantia Book clearly corrects the traditional doctrines of the "fall" and "original sin." Adam and Eve did fall from the high estate of Material Sons to the status of mortal men, but the text says, "⟦Q 75:8.1⟧But that was not the fall of man⟦/Q⟧." [75:8.1] and repeats that there has been no "fall of man" [75:8.2]. The history of mankind is one of progressive evolution, and the Adamic bestowal actually left mankind greatly improved over its previous condition [75:8.2].

1. Mankind Did Not Fall but Rose

Despite Adam's default, mankind was uplifted. The divine plan of giving the violet race miscarried, but the mortal races profited enormously from the limited contribution of Adam and his descendants [75:8.1]. The more superior stocks of Urantia now carry inheritance factors from four sources: Andonite, Sangik, Nodite, and Adamic [75:8.2]. That is why the text says, "⟦Q 75:8.3⟧Adam ne devrait pas être considéré comme une source de malédiction pour la race humaine.⟦/Q⟧." [75:8.3]

2. What Was Lost

This does not mean there was no loss. The default deprived mankind of the full benefit it could have received from the Adamic inheritance [67:7.6], and it also kept mankind from gaining the resistance to disease that Adam's stock had been expected to give [65:5.2]. With Adam's default there also ended the regime of physical representation of the universe government that had lasted more than four hundred and fifty thousand years [76:5.6]. But this is an administrative and social loss, not a guilt inherited by descendants. No one is ever made to suffer vital spiritual deprivation because of the sin of another [67:7.7].

3. An Imperfect Universe and the Glory of Personality

The text says that such missteps are not surprising in an evolutionary universe: "⟦Q 75:8.6⟧Notre univers n’a pas été créé parfait ; la perfection est notre but éternel et non notre origine.⟦/Q⟧." [75:8.6] A mechanical universe would have no friction, but the possibility of disagreement and misunderstanding is evidence that there is personality in the universe, and so we can be sure of the survival, progress, and adventure of personality [75:8.7].

4. Repentance, the Adjusters, and Resurrection

After the second garden was established, Adam and Eve were informed that their repentance had been accepted and that they would qualify for the ranks of the sleeping survivors. Their transgression was an error of judgment, not the sin of conscious rebellion [76:5.1]. Remarkably, shortly after their degradation to mortal status, the combination of a sincerely repentant mind and human status led Thought Adjusters to indwell them, which greatly encouraged them [76:5.2]. Michael sent them a message that they would be called forth from mortal sleep when he came to Urantia [76:5.3]. Adam lived to the age of 530, and Eve died nineteen years before him [76:5.5]. On the third day after Adam's death, in a special resurrection, they were repersonalized on the mansion world together with 1,316 of their associates [76:6.2].

5. From Failure to Triumph

They passed quickly through the ascension worlds and became citizens of Jerusem, returning as sons of man to the place they had left as sons of God, and they are now members of the Twenty-four Counselors [76:6.3]. The text calls this a story of trial, tragedy, and triumph [76:6.4]. Moreover, the darkness of Urantia became the background that led Michael to choose this world as the stage for revealing the Father's love [76:5.7].

Summary

The default of Adam and Eve did not cause mankind to fall; mankind was actually improved by their contribution, and no one inherits their guilt [75:8.1-8.3, 67:7.7]. They themselves repented, received Adjusters, were resurrected, and are now helping Urantia [76:5.2, 76:6.3]. This is a gospel of hope in place of original sin: even for those who have failed, the way of repentance and ascension is open.
